narrative: Argues that the boundary between two interiorities is not a surface but a layered stack of serial transductions — communication itself — and that this stack is fractal, with the same structure of inside-meeting-inside recurring at every scale from synaptic transmission to philosophical dialogue. The chapter distinguishes exterior boundaries (surfaces) from interior boundaries (acts), introduces the boundary-stack as the apparatus through which contact is possible at all, and draws on the OSI model, Koestler's holons, and Mandelbrot's self-similarity to show that the mystery of communication is not failure but that anything gets through.
